subject.title: [Security] Privilege escalation via mock environment overrides in testing framework

question: Does any supported credential-bearing CI or release workflow execute untrusted code that can reach this test environment helper?
rationale: The proposed helper allowlist is not an effective security boundary by itself, while a real privileged workflow path would require security-owner handling and likely workflow-level isolation.

options.title: Require private boundary proof
options.body: Ask for the exact workflow, trigger, secret exposure, and reproducible impact through a private GitHub Security Advisory; close this public issue if that proof is not provided.

options.title: Sponsor defense-in-depth hardening
options.body: Approve a narrow test-hygiene change only as non-security hardening, without claiming it prevents malicious test code from mutating the process environment.

recommendation.title: Require private boundary proof
recommendation.body: Ask for the exact workflow, trigger, secret exposure, and reproducible impact through a private GitHub Security Advisory; close this public issue if that proof is not provided.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history connects this person to both the test-helper integration and repository security policy needed for the boundary decision.
